episodes.172160: A cluster of thunderstorms that developed along a front across South Dakota, moved eastward across west central, and central Minnesota Thursday evening, and early Friday morning. These storms were mainly non-severe with several reports of pea to dime size hail. However, a couple reports of quarter size hail were observed near Madison, over central Lac Qui Parle County, and near Paynesville over Stearns County.
episodes.172584: Thunderstorms pushing offshore from the Volusia and Brevard County coasts produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.173083: Downpours occurred over a portion of leeward Haleakala in East Maui with afternoon heating, leading to flash flooding on the 9th.  More showers developed later over parts of Oahu, Maui, and the Big Island.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.173272: A front settled across the Altamaha River basin into the afternoon and became nearly stationary into the night across the local area as an upper-level impulse passed over the area. High moisture and weak SW steering flow < 10 kts produced locally heavy rainfall, especially near the front into the afternoon and evening.
episodes.173274: A front settled across the Altamaha River basin into the afternoon and became nearly stationary into the night across the local area as an upper-level impulse passed over the area. High moisture and weak SW steering flow < 10 kts produced locally heavy rainfall, especially near the front into the afternoon and evening.
episodes.173275: A brief funnel cloud was spotted near Silver Spring Shores in the afternoon. A surface front lingered cover southeast Georgia with an approaching long wave upper-level trough upstream of the area with SW flow aloft bringing showers and storms across NE FL ahead of the sea breezes over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.174065: Tropical Storm Earl moved north of Puerto Rico early in the month. Although the storm never made landfall, it was responsible for shifting the local wind flow from the south. The islands were under this moist flow for around a week. Adding local effects to the mix, active afternoons were observed, with strong showers and thunderstorms. Several flood and mudslide reports were received.
episodes.174068: Tropical Cyclone Kay formed on September 4th, 2022 and made its closest approach to Southern California on the 9th and 10th, with the center of Kay coming within 120 miles of San Diego. Tropical moisture associated with Kay managed to produce heavy rainfall leading to flooding across mountainous terrain in Southern California on September 9th and 10th. This led to a number of wind damage and flooding events in the mountains and desert foothill locations in Southern California. Kay transitioned to a Post-Tropical Cyclone that weekend, but left enough lingering moisture to support additional rounds of heavy thunderstorms through the 11th and 12th of September. These later rounds of heavy rain would lead to multiple significant debris flow events in the San Bernardino County Mountains, namely in and around the Apple and El Dorado burn scars.
episodes.174069: As Hurricane Earl continued to lift well north of the islands, moisture was still being pulled from the Caribbean into the islands. Therefore, the active weather period continued.
episodes.174163: Tropical Storm Kay moving northward just west of Baja California pushed deep tropical moisture towards southern CA, where objective analysis showed PWATs in excess of 2 inches. Bands of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with the outer bands from the tropical storm affected most of Imperial County, resulting in significant flash flooding.
episodes.174325: Ongoing excessive heat plus a little moisture well ahead of Hurricane Kay fueled isolated thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. One produced severe weather.
episodes.174337: A northeast to southwest-oriented cold front triggered several thunderstorms across east central South Dakota during the evening hours, as it tracked east into warm, humid air. These thunderstorms quickly became severe by producing quarter to half dollar sized hail.
episodes.174531: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind gusts to around 35 knots near Port Aransas.
episodes.174532: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind damage west of Odem.
episodes.174547: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed during the late evening hours of September 9th as an upper level low pressure system evolved over the Gulf of Mexico. Scattered gale-force wind gusts occurred in the western Straits of Florida and Hawk Channel.
episodes.174548: A middle to upper level shortwave trough over the southern Gulf of Mexico moved northeast, enhancing the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms over western Cuba, the western Straits of Florida, and the southeast Gulf of Mexico. Scattered gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with the thunderstorms as they passed over portions of the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.174946: Heavy rainfall across Prince William Sound caused rapid changes in river conditions, along with widespread minor to moderate and low-land flooding, near Cordova and Valdez.

Heavy rainfall caused rapid rises on the Lowe River and surrounding the Solomon Gulch Lake near Valdez, AK. Widespread lowland flooding was reported by the Floodplain Manager as waters rose rapidly during the event, rising as fast as 3 feet in under 12 hours and cresting at 15.02 ft. In doing so, the Lowe River reached moderate flood stage. The Floodplain Manager reported the Lowe River being very high but not on the road. Many low areas near the river were flooded.

Heavy rains across Cordova, AK increased river levels quickly causing areas of minor flooding and lowland overflows in the area. Eyak Lake showed a rapid rise to minor flood stage, however, impacts were limited to flooding along low lying areas and along low roadways. The Eyak Lake river gage crested at 4.81 ft. Portions of the Copper River Highway, connecting Cordova to the airport, had been washed away according to the Cordova Police Department.

No injuries were reported.
